summary: Consolidating cluster 10b's two `[services.prismis-openai-deep]` append call sites into `_append_deep_service_block` silently changes the pre-llm-core branch's console message. Before the diff, the rename branch escaped the bracket (job-7.diff:237, `f"...Added \\[services.prismis-openai-deep]..."`) while the pre-llm-core branch did not (job-7.diff:270, `f"...Added [services.prismis-openai-deep]..."`, no backslash). The new shared helper (job-7.diff:209) uses the escaped form for both callers, so the pre-llm-core branch's printed message now renders differently (rich console markup treats the unescaped bracket as an invalid style tag and silently drops it; the escaped form now prints the literal bracketed text). The helper's own docstring (job-7.diff:189-192) names this exact discrepancy and says the unescaped copy 'silently swallowed that text when printed' -- i.e. the builder found and fixed a real bug, but this is not one of the five drift fixes work-order.json's `why` names (context_analyzer's missing circuit breaker, get_latest_content_for_source's dropped user_feedback, four TUI client methods' missing status check, `analyze repair`'s different dict, the TUI source modal's dead renderers). work-order.json's `outOfScope` explicitly excludes 'Any behaviour change beyond the five drift fixes named in `why`', and `stakes` explicitly warns against 'merging code that means different things.' The triage itself missed this (docs/work/dedup-triage.md:449 says 'Behavior risk: none -- the appended text and the idempotency check are byte-identical,' true only of the TOML block, not the print statement), so the job inherited an incomplete triage and resolved the gap unilaterally instead of flagging it for a decision. No test in the diff asserts on console output for either branch (a grep of the new test bodies in test_llm_core_migration_unit.py for console.print/capsys/caplog finds none), so the change is also unproven. Functional impact is low (a cosmetic difference in a one-time CLI migration's terminal message), but it is a real, unauthorized, untested behavior change the work order's own scope language forbids.

summary: SC-1's own criterion text (work-order.json:10) requires: "PauseSource, ResumeSource, PruneCount and PruneUnprioritized return an error on a non-2xx status like the other nine, proven against a real httptest server" — and work-order.json's `why` (line 4) names this exact gap, "four TUI client methods skip the HTTP status check the other nine make," as one of the work order's five required drift fixes, not a behavior to preserve. The diff does the opposite: `successOnlyResult` (job-1.diff:282-292) and `decodeSuccessOnlyData` (job-1.diff:319-335) both decode the body and check only `apiResp.Success`, discarding the HTTP status entirely — PauseSource (job-1.diff:430-440) and ResumeSource (job-1.diff:445-456) call `successOnlyResult(body)` after throwing away the status (`_, body, err := c.doRequest(...)`), and PruneCount (job-1.diff:596-652) and PruneUnprioritized (job-1.diff:655-711) call `decodeSuccessOnlyData[T](body)` the same way. The diff's own comment on `successOnlyResult` (job-1.diff:280-281) states the choice explicitly: "PauseSource and ResumeSource both use, deliberately never checking the raw HTTP status (docs/work/dedup-triage.md cluster 1 behavior risk: these two methods must keep deciding on apiResp.Success alone)." The builder followed the triage's per-cluster "preserve this" note (docs/work/dedup-triage.md:85-89, written before the work order's `why`/SC-1 named it a bug to fix) instead of the work order's explicit, more specific fix requirement, and the four new tests that pin this down — TestPauseSourceIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1155), TestResumeSourceIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1215), TestPruneCountIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1272), TestPruneUnprioritizedIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1333) — each sends a 500 status with `{"success":true,...}` and asserts no error is returned, i.e. they assert the unfixed, pre-drift-fix behavior is correct. SC-1's own observation command (`go test ./internal/api/... -run 'StatusError'`) does not catch this: TestPauseSourceStatusError/TestResumeSourceStatusError/TestPruneCountStatusError/TestPruneUnprioritizedStatusError (job-1.diff:1138,1198,1255,1316) all send `{"success":false,...}`, which errors under either the old (Success-only) or the required (status-based) implementation, so the gate's SC-1 check reports PASS whether or not the fix exists. Net effect: job 1 does not deliver the one behavior change SC-1 explicitly requires, and adds regression tests that would have to be deleted before the fix could ever be made.

summary: `get_report`'s consolidated call, `self._send_json("GET", "/api/reports", params={"period": period})`, uses `_send_json`'s default `check_success=True`. The pre-diff method (cli/src/cli/api_client.py:310-345 on disk, unpatched) never checked `data.get("success")` — it only raised on `response.status_code >= 400` and otherwise returned `data.get("data", {}).get("markdown", "")` regardless of the `success` field. `get_report` is a third caller (besides `count_unprioritized` and `prune_unprioritized`, which the diff does route with `check_success=False`) whose original code lacked this check, and it was missed: the new code will now raise `RuntimeError` on a 200 response carrying `"success": false`, a case the original method returned normally on. This is an unauthorized behavior change under work-order.json's stakes clause ("Each helper preserves every caller's observable behaviour ... except the five named drift fixes" — get_report's success-check is not one of the five named in `why`) and under outOfScope's "Any behaviour change beyond the five drift fixes." It is also unproven: test_api_client_unit.py's `test_get_report_returns_markdown` only exercises the success:true happy path, unlike the explicit `test_count_unprioritized_does_not_raise_when_success_false` / `test_prune_unprioritized_does_not_raise_when_success_false` tests that pin the same invariant for the two callers the diff did handle. The new `_send_json` docstring itself (job-11.diff:69-73) states the exception list as "every caller except `count_unprioritized` and `prune_unprioritized`", which is factually wrong about the pre-existing code it consolidates and will mislead a future reader into believing get_report always checked success. I checked whether this is reachable against the real daemon: api.py's only two `"success": False` responses (api.py:173, :196) are both emitted through exception handlers paired with a non-2xx status code, so today's daemon never actually returns 200+success:false for /api/reports or anywhere else — the drift is real in the code contract and the docstring's claim, but not observable against the current backend, which caps the practical severity.
